rationales.F01: Acute, severe precordial chest pain radiating to the left arm is highly suggestive of Acute Myocardial Infarction.
rationales.F02: Similar chest pain at rest that resolved spontaneously is more indicative of Unstable Angina, but also possible in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
rationales.F09: Elevated serum troponin I level is a strong indicator of Acute Myocardial Infarction and rules out Unstable Angina.
rationales.F10: 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery is a strong indicator of Acute Myocardial Infarction and rules out Unstable Angina.

frontier_selector.why: The elevated serum troponin I level and hypomotility in the anterior wall, which are specific to myocardial damage, decided it.
